facts.fact_text: The applicants held numerous public meetings at Tbilisi State University as part of their activities opposing the reforms.
On 19 June 2006 the already-dissolved Grand Academic Council organised a meeting of Tbilisi State University staff.

After the meeting with Mr G.Kh. ended without results, Tbilisi State University employees — including all of the applicants — decided to stay at the University in one of the lecture halls and hold a further meeting among themselves.
On 20 June 2006 the applicants, along with other employees of Tbilisi State University, gathered again in one of the lecture halls of the University.
At the meeting of 3 July 2006, the already-dissolved Grand Academic Council 'elected' the second applicant as the new Rector of Tbilisi State University.

After the 'election' of the second applicant as new Rector, a group of about twenty people, including all of the applicants, headed to the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh. to inform him of the Grand Academic Council's decision and to demand his resignation.

According to the case file, after their removal from the acting Rector's office, the applicants together with other protesters — totalling approximately 400 people — gathered in one of the lecture halls of the main Tbilisi State University building and continued their protest.
According to the applicants, the police forced everyone out of the Tbilisi State University building without giving any explanations or prior warning.
Towards the evening of 20 June 2006 the police allegedly again dispersed the applicants' meeting at Tbilisi State University.
While the meeting at acting Rector Mr G.Kh.'s office continued, the police entered the Tbilisi State University grounds.
According to the applicants, after the police asked the applicants and others present to leave the acting Rector's office, they left without any resistance and moved to a lecture hall.
The applicants alleged that at around 11 p.m. on 3 July 2006 the police closed the doors of the lecture hall and prevented the people inside from leaving.
The applicants alleged that they had been locked in the lecture hall without access to water, food or toilet facilities until approximately 8-10 a.m. on 4 July 2006.

By a decision of 4 August 2006, the Tbilisi City Court found the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, seventh and eighth applicants guilty of administrative offences under Articles 166, 173 and 174 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Tbilisi City Court imposed a fine of 100 Georgian laris (approximately 45 euros) on each of the first, second, third, fourth, fifth, seventh and eighth applicants.

Article 166 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, as in force at the material time, defined minor hooliganism (a minor breach of public order) as swearing and cursing in a public place, causing insulting harassment to a person, or other similar actions which disturb public order and peace, punishable by a fine of 100 Georgian laris or, if that measure was not deemed sufficient, up to thirty days' administrative detention.

Article 173 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, as in force at the material time, provided that maliciously disobeying a lawful instruction or order issued by a law enforcement officer shall be punishable by a fine amounting to ten times the minimum monthly wage, or by one to six months' correctional labour compounded by the withholding of 20% of the offender's wages, or, if those measures were not deemed sufficient, by up to thirty days' administrative detention.

Article 174 of the Code of Administrative Offences of Georgia, as in force at the material time, defined arbitrary behaviour as the exercise of a right in violation of a law which does not cause any significant damage to people, the State or to public bodies, punishable by a warning or a fine of half the minimum monthly wage, or in the case of public officials, a warning or a fine of one minimum monthly wage.

Under Article 9 of the Law on the Police, as in force at the material time, the police were responsible inter alia for dispersing unlawful rallies, demonstrations, pickets and other assemblies that posed a threat to public safety, the lives and health of people, property, and other rights guaranteed by law.

In connection with the charge of a minor breach of public order (minor hooliganism), the Tbilisi City Court established that the applicants had burst into the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh., calling for his resignation.

The Tbilisi City Court concluded that the applicants' behaviour had amounted to insulting harassment with respect to Mr G.Kh. and other staff present, and to 'other similar action' that had violated public order and peace.
According to the applicants, despite the applicants' repeated requests, the police officers did not show them any order authorising the removal of the people gathered at Tbilisi State University.
According to the applicants, they entered acting Rector Mr G.Kh.'s office on 3 July 2006 without using any force and informed him of the Grand Academic Council's decision.
According to the applicants, after the police asked the applicants and others present to leave the acting Rector's office, they left without any resistance and moved to a lecture hall.
The applicants alleged that at around 11 p.m. on 3 July 2006 the police closed the doors of the lecture hall and prevented the people inside from leaving.
The applicants alleged that they had been locked in the lecture hall without access to water, food or toilet facilities until approximately 8-10 a.m. on 4 July 2006.

At the hearing of 3 August 2006, police patrol officer G.Ch. clarified in reply to a question that no one had physically resisted the police, but that the protesters had simply refused to leave the acting Rector's office.

The two journalists and two professors questioned on 3 August 2006 all claimed that there had been no confrontation — either physical or verbal — in the office of acting Rector Mr G.Kh. on 3 July 2006.

The two journalists and two professors questioned on 3 August 2006 claimed that the group had been simply demanding the resignation of Mr G.Kh. and that they had left the office at the request of the police.
On 4 September 2006, the chairwoman of the Tbilisi Court of Appeal, sitting privately and without holding an oral hearing, dismissed the applicants' appeal as unsubstantiated.
